# ElevenLabs Prompt — Weary Detective Noir Narration

## Voice Direction

**Voice profile:** Middle-aged, deep, slightly gravelly baritone. Think a 1940s–50s hardboiled P.I. — Bogart-esque cadence, but world-worn and softer around the edges. Speak slowly, deliberately, with the weight of someone who has seen too much and slept too little.

**Delivery notes:**
- Tone is sardonic, melancholic, dry-witted — the kind of voice that lights a cigarette between sentences.
- Allow slight breathiness and tired pauses, especially after reflective lines.
- Emphasize metaphors and similes; let descriptions of the city breathe.
- Lower the volume slightly on introspective moments; raise it only slightly on cynical asides, as if smirking to himself.

---

## Narration Text

> The rain hadn't stopped in three days, and neither had I. Not drinking, no — I'd given that up after the Ashford case — just sitting. Watching the neon bleed across the wet sidewalk. Outside, the city writes its own kind of poetry. Mine just got the punctuation wrong.
>
> She walked in at quarter past eleven. Blonde hair, red dress, and a story that smelled like trouble and cheap perfume. I didn't want to take the case. I never do. But trouble has a way of finding a man who owes it money, and I was three months behind on what I owed her.
>
> She said her husband was missing. I told her most husbands are. She didn't find that funny. A dame like that rarely does.
>
> I poured two fingers of bourbon I said I wasn't drinking and lit a cigarette I said I'd quit. The lamp on my desk flickered like it was trying to tell me something. It should've tried harder.
>
> Outside, a siren wailed down the alley. Inside, she sat down across from me, crossed her legs, and waited for an answer I didn't have yet.
>
> I took a long drag and stared at the rain.
>
> "Tell me about your husband," I said. "And start with the lie."

---

**Tip for ElevenLabs:** Paste the *Voice Direction* block into the "Voice Settings" prompt or style notes field, and the scene text into the main input. For added effect, enable "Stability" around 35–45% and "Similarity" around 70% to encourage natural, slightly raspy expressiveness rather than flat delivery.
